title: Arabic greetings and script
examples: How do I say hello in Arabic?
Does Arabic write from left to right?
What is the hardest part about Arabic letters?

explain.say: Today we will learn some basic Arabic greetings.
Arabic script is written from right to left.
Arabic letters have a special way of joining together.
When letters join, the shape of the letter changes.
In real life, you see this when reading Arabic signs.
A common mistake is writing the letters separately.

faq.a: No, Arabic script is written from the right side to the left side. You can also ask, 'What is the writing direction for Arabic?' or 'Which way should I read Arabic?'

faq.q: Do the letters always look different when they join?
faq.a: Yes, most Arabic letters change their shape depending on where they are in a word. You might ask, 'How do letters change shape?' or 'What is the rule for joining letters?'
'Marhaba' is a common and friendly way to say hello in Arabic. You could also ask, 'What is the Arabic greeting?' or 'How do I say hello?'

faq.q: Is the script always written from right to left?
faq.a: Yes, for standard Arabic, the writing direction is consistently from right to left. Another way to ask is, 'From which side does Arabic start?'
asks: Does it always go right to left?

faq.q: Do I have to learn all the letter changes?
faq.a: You need to notice that the shape changes, but don't worry about memorizing everything at once. Just focus on the joining concept. You can ask, 'Is it too hard to learn?'

facts: Arabic is written from right to left.
Arabic letters change shape when they connect.
Joining letters is a key feature of the script.

quiz.why: Arabic writing always begins on the right side of the page.

wrong.0: This is the direction used for English writing.

options.show: They only join at the start
